say.t: The room is the same as yesterday. The rain has eased a little; the drops on the window stay where they are.
Last night's speck of light denies it was ever there, now that it is light.
The glass of water is still on the desk, cold.
The loose one in the case. An instant camera, a cream-white shell, a red shutter.
The little window on the back says: 10. Ten sheets left.
You pick up the chick and turn it over. That small hole, black.
Poking it never did anything, back then. You poke it anyway.
The plastic springs back. Same as back then.
The small window in the bottom right is lit. You do not lie down straight away.
Before turning the screens off you open the afternoon's document once more.
One line is gone. A line you added yourself: this field may have no aliases.
It is not in the history either. You do not write it again.
One line missing. And it had to be that one.
Before sleep you pick the instant camera up again. The shutter is as stiff as ever.
The last summer of primary school. The back door of the classroom is open; the sun reaches all the way to the teacher's desk.
You didn't really know how to talk to people then. The camera was yours to bring to school: the windowsill, the blackboard, the empty corridor.
A week before graduation, somebody noticed it. You never knew who was first.
Hey, this thing prints the photo right away? Take one of me!
Okay. Stand still.
No, no, give me the camera, I'll take one of you.
You hand it over. She lifts it and presses. The sheet is half out when she tugs it free.
Me! Me next!
Line up! One each!
The camera goes from this hand to that one. You stand at the edge and watch it travel.
How many left?
Ten. Nine now.
Hey, you too. Stand in the middle!
You step in. Someone counts to three, someone shouts cheese, a flash.
It's coming up, it's coming up. Oh. Your eyes are shut.
One more! ... This one, that's half your shoulder.
No sheets left. Never mind, next time.
There was no next time. The photos from that day were shared out, one each, everyone else's face on them.
In junior high you wrote to a few of them. The addresses were copied down on graduation day.
Nobody wrote back.
Dozens of photos. Not one with me in it.
Today is over.
The file sits where I sent it. Wang received it and nothing since.

items.text: Help Xiao Zhang: take Vivi's page apart.

say.t: Ding-dong.

items.text: One box in the case is loose. Take it out.
Take a look at the desk.
